parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Today I'm going to introduce a small island called St. Ninian Isle, which lies off the coast of the Shetland Islands in Northern Scotland. Although it is quite small, it has become extremely important for historians and archaeologists because of several fascinating discoveries made there.
Let's begin with the physical landscape of the island. Along this part of Scotland's coastline, there are a number of narrow sea inlets cutting into the land. In the local Scottish dialect, people use a special word to describe this kind of coastal feature. The term voe is used locally and it refers to what most English speakers would simply call a bay. Another interesting point about the island today is that it does not have a permanent population anymore. No one lives there throughout the year. However, the island is far from empty because it supports a wide variety of wildlife, particularly sea birds that nest along the cliffs and rocky shores. These animals are now the island's most common inhabitants, meaning the place is largely populated by birds.
Moving on to the archaeological findings, researchers have carried out several excavations in the ruins of early religious buildings on the island. During these investigations, they uncovered many remains that were clearly human. Among the discoveries were numerous bones, which provided valuable evidence about the people who once lived and worshipped there. Perhaps the most famous discovery, however, was made not by a professional archaeologist but by a local schoolboy. While exploring the island, he came across a small wooden container buried in the ground. When it was open, researchers found that every object inside had been made from the same precious metal. All of the items were crafted from silver, which immediately suggested that the collection was extremely valuable.
Now let's look more closely at the objects discovered inside the wooden box, because these items tell us a great deal about the people who owned them. First of all, the fact that the objects were made of precious metal immediately suggested that the owner was not an ordinary individual. Items like these would have required considerable wealth, and therefore archaeologists believe that the person who possessed them must have held a relatively high status within the local community.
When researchers examined the contents of the box more carefully, they discovered a group of eating vessels. Researchers counted eight pieces of tableware in total, most of which were small bowls. Most were probably used for everyday meals, although one was noticeably larger, and may have been intended for ceremonial purposes.
Another particularly interesting item was a spoon with a decorated handle. At the end of the handle, craftsmen had carved the image of an animal. The design clearly represented a dog, and the carving showed the animal's head, a decorative style that can still be seen in later metalwork traditions.
In addition to the bowls and spoons, archaeologists identified another unusual object among the collection. It was a small metal implement whose exact purpose is still debated. However, based on its shape and design, experts believe it functioned as a small tool designed to remove shellfish from their shells while eating.
For many years, researchers assumed that the collection of objects must have belonged to a church, since the items were discovered close to the ruins of religious buildings. However, more recent interpretations suggest a different explanation. The style and variety of the objects indicate that they were probably part of a private collection owned by a family, rather than property belonging to the church itself.
The final mystery concerns why the items were hidden in the first place. Archaeologists believe that the owners deliberately buried the box in order to protect their valuables. At that time, communities in the region sometimes faced raids or attacks, so it is likely that the people who hid the treasure believed they were in danger and hoped to return later to retrieve it. Unfortunately, it seems that they never came back, leaving the treasure to remain hidden for centuries until it was eventually rediscovered.

录音明确提到现在岛上的主要居民（inhabitants）是鸟类（birds）。
填 seabirds 也可以，seabirds 也可以写成一个词。

录音提到在遗迹中发现了大量人类遗骸，紧接着具体指出的就是很多骨头（bones）。

听到“precious metal”时不要慌着乱猜，注意听后面“crafted from”跟着的具体材质才是答案。
录音说明盒子里所有由珍贵金属制作的物品全是用银（silver）打造的。

录音明确说到拥有这些贵重物品的人在当地社区中一定拥有较高的地位（status）。
录音提到这八件餐具中大部分是小碗（bowls），且分别提到了它们的日常和仪式用途。

When researchers examined the contents of the box more carefully, they discovered a group of eating vessels. Researchers counted eight pieces of tableware in total, most of which were small bowls. Most were probably used for everyday meals, although one was noticeably larger, and may have been intended for ceremonial purposes.

Another particularly interesting item was a spoon with a decorated handle. At the end of the handle, craftsmen had carved the image of an animal. The design clearly represented a dog, and the carving showed the animal's head, a decorative style that can still be seen in later metalwork traditions.
你可能听到了“image”或“design”，但题目问的是动物的哪个具体部位（animal's...），对应录音中清清楚楚的“animal's head”。
录音指出勺子手柄上雕刻的狗的图案，具体展示的是动物的头部（head）。

In addition to the bowls and spoons, archaeologists identified another unusual object among the collection. It was a small metal implement whose exact purpose is still debated. However, based on its shape and design, experts believe it functioned as a small tool designed to remove shellfish from their shells while eating.
你可能听到了前面的“implement”或“object”，但录音后面清晰解释了“functioned as a small tool”才是直接对应题目“possibly used when eating...”的核心词。
录音提到专家认为那个用来吃贝类的小金属器具，其实就是一个小工具（tool）。

However, more recent interpretations suggest a different explanation. The style and variety of the objects indicate that they were probably part of a private collection owned by a family, rather than property belonging to the church itself.

录音明确指出这些物品是一户家庭（family）的私人收藏，而不是教堂的财产。

At that time, communities in the region sometimes faced raids or attacks, so it is likely that the people who hid the treasure believed they were in danger and hoped to return later to retrieve it.
你可能听到了“raids”或“attacks”，但它们不符合题目“in...”的介词搭配，录音直接给出了“in danger”这个固定表达。
录音解释当时社区面临袭击，所以藏宝的人认为自己身处危险之中（in danger）。
